findings.title: Existing V2 realms never receive the new Clients resource or scopes
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. A realm that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retains only the old Users resource and scopes after upgrade; it never gets the Clients resource or the configure/map-roles client scopes. Creating a Clients permission will fail scope validation, and `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` can reach the missing all-clients resource path. Reconcile/create missing schema scopes and resource-type resources for an existing admin-permissions client instead of returning unconditionally.

findings.title: The all-clients manage scope does not permit listing clients
findings.body: `canView()` only considers the legacy view roles and the V2 `view` scope, while the inherited `canList()` contract is based on `canView()` (or query roles). A caller granted only the new all-clients `manage` scope can manage/view a known client through `canView(ClientModel)`, but cannot call the client list endpoint. This also contradicts the new `testManageAllClients`, which expects `findAll()` to succeed after granting only `manage`. Include the all-clients manage grant in the realm-level view/list decision, consistent with the per-client transitive behavior.

findings.title: V2 drops built-in manage-clients access for role mapping
findings.body: The overrides for `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate the new authorization scopes. Unlike the inherited evaluator, they do not preserve the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role shortcut. Consequently an administrator with the standard `realm-management/manage-clients` role loses the ability to map client roles, manage composites, and map client-scope roles whenever FGAP V2 is enabled, unless separately granted new schema permissions. Retain the legacy admin-role check before evaluating V2 scopes.

findings.title: Per-client resources are created without the Clients resource type
findings.body: When a permission targets one client, the schema creates a resource and assigns scopes but never assigns `resourceType` to it. `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission()` subsequently uses `resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and therefore cannot discover these individual client resources. Any caller using that method will treat client-specific grants as absent. Set the resource type when creating an object resource (as is already done for the all-resource entry during initialization).

findings.title: Client deletion skips V2 permission-resource cleanup
findings.body: The removal listener is now gated by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, but V2 authorization is selected using the distinct `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature. In a V2-only deployment the listener does nothing when a target client is deleted, leaving its per-client authorization resource and policies in the admin-permissions resource server permanently orphaned. If both flags are enabled, the listener instead selects `ClientPermissionsV2` and calls its `setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Add V2-specific cleanup for deleted target clients and gate it on the V2 feature rather than suppressing the event.

findings.title: Void require-view methods are documented as returning a boolean
findings.body: The Javadoc above `requireView()` says it "Returns true" even though the method is `void`; the same incorrect statement is repeated above `requireViewClientScopes()` at line 101. These methods should document that they throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding capability is absent, as the other `require*` methods do.
